game: CLE@NYJ Week 5 2026 (kickoff time not in pack; NYJ home, outdoor assumed only as venue type, forecast not saved)

script.base: No spread or total was saved, so this is a form script, not a market script. Both defenses bleed the middle (NYJ 9.26 YPA on 35 throws, CLE 9.47 on 30) and CLE has allowed more explosives (15 passes of 20+ for 156 yards vs NYJ 9/136), so the base lean is competitive and pass-skewed: Watson keeps a designed-run share (19/95 in weeks 2-4) while Judkins grinds inefficient volume (47/144, 3.06 YPC), and NYJ still funnels through Wilson (24 targets, 191 yards) with Allen, not Hall, as the rush chair.
script.flip1: NYJ's 37% blitz plus Teven Jenkins (G) out turns CLE into a quick game: Fannin and the RBs catch more, Boston's 14.9 aDOT (269 air yards on 18 targets) stalls, and sack yardage can cut Watson's rush line even if he scrambles.
script.flip2: CLE's three DTs out (Mason Graham, Mike Hall Jr., Kalia Davis) let NYJ run through Allen and steal late snaps from Wilson and Isaiah Williams; if CLE is the one that leads, Judkins' carries rise and the pass volume that Fannin needs dries up.

injury_fallout: Known pre-kick from the pack injury report, not inactives. CLE: Dillon Gabriel Out so Deshaun Watson is the QB; Carsen Ryan Out so Harold Fannin Jr. does not split TE snaps (Whiteheart only 2 targets in weeks 2-4); Tylan Wallace Out is minor with Jeudy already at 4 targets; Teven Jenkins Out should raise pressure, cut Judkins' efficiency, and push quick throws. NYJ: Breece Hall Out (29 carries, 61 yards, 8 targets, 86 yards in weeks 2-4) so Braelon Allen is the rush chair and Isaiah Davis (rush line 14.5, no prior games, team tag missing) is the vulture risk; Adonai Mitchell Out removes 12 targets and 178 air yards, with Wilson, Isaiah Williams and Kenyon Sadiq the absorbers; Dylan Parham Out weakens the NYJ run/pass pro; Francisco Mauigoa (LB) Out helps CLE TEs, RBs and short/middle targets. Questionable, not confirmed: Tim Patrick, Kingsley Enagbare, Will McDonald IV. CLE DT outs are the run-defense hole for Allen.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting, no MOFO/MOFC or man/zone rate in the pack. Location splits are the shell proxy: NYJ is stingy outside (left 5.83 YPA on 42, right 5.06 on 50) and soft in the middle (9.26 on 35); CLE is soft everywhere and worst in the middle (left 6.19 on 59, middle 9.47 on 30, right 6.69 on 55).
matchup.pressure: NYJ blitz 37%; CLE EPA/db is 0.13 vs blitz and 0.15 vs none, so the blitz has not crushed this offense in the saved sample, but Jenkins out is the unquantified pressure add (no pressure rate or sack log saved). CLE blitzes only 25%; NYJ EPA/db is 0.15 vs blitz and 0.13 vs none, a slight positive, not a pressure kill on Wilson.
matchup.bleeds: NYJ bleeds the middle, not the edges, and has allowed only 9 passes of 20+ (136 yards) and a 4.50 rush YPC with 12 runs of 10+. CLE bleeds explosives and the middle, and the run front is worse on paper today with three DTs out (season 4.75 YPC, 15 runs of 10+).
matchup.overlap: CLE's volume that actually attacks NYJ's weak middle is Fannin (20 targets, 130 air yards, 6.5 aDOT) and Concepcion (23 targets, 4.8 aDOT), not Boston (14.9 aDOT into the edges NYJ defends). Mauigoa out is the LB piece of that overlap. NYJ's overlap is Wilson (9.9 aDOT, 24 targets) into CLE's explosive/middle bleed, clouded by Mitchell being out (more targets or more brackets) and by the DT outs inviting a run script.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Fannin is the CLE piece who actually attacks the only zone NYJ bleeds — the middle at 9.26 YPA — and today he gets a 37% blitz, Mauigoa out, Ryan out, and Jenkins out pushing quick throws, against a 35-yard line that sits under his 44-yard weeks 2-4 pace.
edge_players.must_be_true: Fannin keeps a full TE1 snap share with Carsen Ryan out, Watson gets to the quick game (about 6-7 targets, not a sack-fest), and NYJ does not suddenly take the middle away.
edge_players.kills_it: A CLE lead that turns into Judkins clock-killing, a blank like the 21-yard game, or the blitz getting home so often that targets dump to Judkins/Sanders instead of Fannin. No two-sided price is saved, so a juiced or moved number also kills the bet.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Fannin over 35 lost because NYJ, already only 0.02 EPA/db worse for CLE when they blitz, sat a safety in the middle after Mauigoa went down and Watson, without Jenkins, checked to Judkins (14 targets, 79 yards in weeks 2-4) instead of the TE. The 21- and 27-yard games are half the last4, the 35 was never a real two-sided market, and a CLE lead let Judkins (47 carries in three games) kill the clock. That counter is why this is a lean and a flag, not a strong bet. Allen under 71.5 was the other finalist and was passed: even a full Hall inheritance is only about 16 carries, but 16 at the 4.75 CLE allows is already 76, and three starting DTs are out, so the counter-case is at least as strong as the number gap.
slip_story: One-story slip only: CLE quick-game versus a 37% blitz and a middle-bleeding NYJ defense. Fannin over is the sole leg. Do not add Judkins rush over, Allen rush over, a game under, or Boston deep over — those need a run clock, a NYJ grind against the backup DTs, or outside explosives. No TD legs, no second market on Fannin, and no 3-4 leg slip was built because the second candidate did not survive the pre-mortem.
